title: Canonicalize weight manifest, shard coalescer, and vocab-binding to shorten model bootstrap tail
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Model bootstrap time is skewed by a large number of tiny weight shards and inconsistent weight manifest formats. The runtime spends significant time opening many small files, validating format variants, and performing repeated tokenizer handshakes for lexicon variants. This causes tail latency spikes for cold-starts and model-activation-heavy workloads (seen on Dedicated pools and Private customers).

Goal: Deliver a low-risk refactor that: (1) introduces a canonical weight manifest format and a deterministic migration path from existing manifests, (2) implements a shard coalescer that produces runtime-friendly blob segments (coalesced shards with index offsets) to reduce I/O and metadata overhead, and (3) replaces ad-hoc tokenizer handshakes with a small 'vocab-binding' shim that normalizes tokenizer metadata across formats.

Scope: runtime manifest parser, ingestion pipeline (ingest service), model registry migration, runtime loader changes (read-only runtime to consume coalesced segments), and test harness + perf dashboards. Backwards compatibility: ingest service will produce canonical manifests and coalesced segments; runtime supports a compatibility fallback to legacy manifests for 3 months after rollout.

Deliverables: design doc, canonical manifest schema, ingest-service coalescer implementation, runtime loader adapter, unit + integration tests, migration tool (CLI), perf dashboard showing 95/99/99.9th bootstrap latency, rollout plan and canary settings.
comments: 2026-02-25 - Aisha Raman: Created after spike (perf/2026-02-22) showed >3x tail on bootstrap for models with >1k weight shards. Captured sample traces and S3 key distributions. Design doc skeleton at Confluence (link below).

2026-02-27 - Diego Morales: Compatibility matrix completed for safetensors, ckpt-v2, legacy-ckpt, and custom-index. Coalescer approach chosen: preserve original checksums at segment-level, produce a lightweight manifest that maps logical tensors -> (segment_id, offset, length). This avoids re-serializing tensors unnecessarily.

2026-03-02 - Eng Arch Review (Bethany Chu): Approved schema with one requested change: include a per-segment 'activation_hint' byte to allow runtime prefetch heuristics. Also asked for an explicit migration rollback plan.

2026-03-04 - Diego: Implemented initial ingest-side coalescer prototype (branch: feature/eng/ENG-481209-coalescer). Local perf: 60% reduction in open calls and 25% lower cold activation 95th. Pushed PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5467 (WIP).

2026-03-06 - QA (Liam O'Connor): Integration smoke ran against mixed-format bundles. Found edge-case: models that embed multiple tokenizer vocab variants in vocab.json require deterministic merging; patched coalescer to emit separate 'vocab_bindings' entries and added verification step.

2026-03-09 - Aisha: Updated ticket with rollout plan and canary thresholds. Next: runtime adapter for coalesced segments, add dashboard panels for file-open calls per-activation, and prepare migration CLI to produce canonical manifests in bulk.

acceptance_criteria:
- Ingest service writes canonical manifest and coalesced segments for new uploads.
- Runtime loader can consume coalesced segments and fallback to legacy manifests.
- Bootstrap 95th latency reduced by >=20% on representative models.
- Migration CLI can convert at least 95% of existing bundles without tensor mutation.
- Tests (unit + integration) added and passing in CI.
- Rollout plan with canary and automatic fallback in case of errors.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (canary): ingest new bundles with canonical manifests in dedicated staging for 2 weeks; monitor open-call and bootstrap latency; Phase 2: enable coalesced segment reads in runtime for 10% of traffic with automatic fallback; Phase 3: run offline migration CLI for high-impact buckets and offer optional bulk migration to customers; Phase 4: deprecate legacy manifest support after 3 months once telemetry is stable.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Corrupt coalesced segment indices could cause activation failures. Mitigation: include per-segment checksum and conservative validation in runtime loader; ship adapter that falls back.
Risk: Tokenizer vocab merges may change token ids for custom vocab formats. Mitigation: vocab-binding shim produces deterministic id-mapping and includes a validation layer in ingest; flag models for manual review if merge is ambiguous.
Risk: Migration at scale could stress object store. Mitigation: rate-limit migration CLI and prioritize hot-models; run migration from colocated workers to minimize egress.
